parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction: no trans-specific record, so I extrapolate from documented anti-gender-nonconforming hostility (a 2010 killing, slurs against effeminate men, evangelical campaigns against gay tourists) and police dismissiveness (2019 refusal to investigate, victims ridiculed) — societal hostility with thin recourse (tier 3), no universal-exposure measure, no organised targeting, no trans-specific offence. Positives carry weight: functioning courts reading down the sodomy provisions (2024), a sustained advocacy/challenge record, 2011 UN violence-declaration signatory, a bishop opposing criminalisation and violence. Negative material is largely dated (2009–2011), and the police lever from sexuality law is substantially weakened by the 2024 reading-down, though sections remain on the books. No facility, document or custody rule is documented either way — open questions, not exposures. Friction, violence risk and absent protections place it in Elevated Risk.
